BombVault has a new interface. Everything 9.9.1 could do is still there, in fewer places: five entries in the sidebar, one list for everything that is backed up, and settings as tiles. Pictures show how 3-2-1, retention, the relay and the emergency restore work, and a ZFS dataset can keep a block-exact replica on a second ZFS host.

## ✨ Added

### Backups: one list for everything

- **One list.** Containers, VMs, folders, the flash drive and ZFS datasets stand in one list. Tiles above it pick a kind, and they select instead of hiding the rest of the page.
- **Filter, Sort and Search** are three buttons above the list. Sort goes by name, status, last backup, size or schedule, in both directions.
- **The last runs as a strip.** A row shows its last fourteen runs as small squares and one status. Everything else about it is in the info bubble beside its name.
- **Select like in a file manager**, with Ctrl+click, Shift+click and Ctrl+A, and a right-click menu on every row. A row's buttons appear when the pointer is over it.
- **Add from one window**: a folder or a ZFS dataset, with the system configuration offered as a suggestion.

### A page for every entry

- **Three tabs**: **Backups**, **Settings** and **Verify**, under a flat header with the name, one line of state and the actions.
- **Backups** lists the entry's backups with a bar per day, the storage locations that hold them, the size by folder and the last runs.
- **Settings** holds the schedule and storage location, exclude patterns, commands before and after, other containers to stop, database dumps, stacks, former names and the folders that are backed up. Schedule, retention and storage locations follow the default until the entry gets a value of its own.
- **Verify** shows the checks, the entry's anomalies and its repository.

### Restore

- **One page.** Pick a section, search for what you want back and choose a backup from a list with the newest at the top. A handle on the list's rail drags from one backup to the next.
- **The emergency restore and other sources** stand beside it: another instance, or an old backup folder with its recovery kit.
- **The window asks in steps** and plays the scene of the target you picked. The safe choice is preselected: next to the original and not over it.

### Anomalies

- **Tiles for Critical, Warnings and Notes**, with Open and Closed above the list.
- **A finding offers its fix first**, and its details show the value as a curve over the usual range.
- **Learning progress.** When nothing is open, a ring per entry shows how far the detection has learned what is normal.

### The overview

- **Five cards to start with**: the status, what needs you, the protection of each section, the storage locations with a forecast of when they fill up, and the history with runs and log.
- **The other cards wait under Customize**: anomalies, not backed up, the calendar, storage, the summary, statistics and the host integration. Every card can be moved, resized and hidden.
- **The ring in the head** shows how much is protected and turns into a progress ring with its stations while a backup runs.
- **One count everywhere.** Every card counts entries the same way.

### Pictures that explain

- **3-2-1 as a flow.** Every line from a section to a place is a switch, and **Graphic / Switches** brings back the plain table.
- **Retention as a timeline** that shows which backups a rule keeps.
- **A fill level as a vessel**, with the mark where the place is full.
- **The week as a band**, with every planned run from Monday to Sunday.
- **Scenes** for pairing, the relay, the emergency restore, encryption, database dumps, deduplication, the off-site copy, the delete protection and the checks. They stand still when motion is switched off.

### Instances and pairing

- **Every instance is paired through the phrase.** Three step cards show how, and a finished pairing is confirmed on the page.
- **A card per instance** with its roles as tiles: **Receiver**, **Fetcher** and **ZFS server**. An info bubble says how the roles differ, a request shows on the card as a badge, and **Details** opens the rest.
- **The group as a net** shows who does what for whom. A role that still waits is dashed.
- **The relay in four forms**, each with its picture, a paired BombVault among them.
- **A ZFS server without BombVault** is connected over SSH from the same place.

### ZFS replica

- **A second copy as real datasets.** A ZFS entry can replicate to a ZFS server over SSH or to a paired BombVault, after every backup or on a schedule of its own, with its own retention on the target (#320).
- **Incremental and resumable.** A run sends only what changed, and an interrupted stream continues where it stopped.
- **Bring it back as a new dataset**, or clone a snapshot on the target with the commands the page shows.
- **A paired instance has to allow it**, with a pool, a root and a retention rule, and can take the permission away again.
- **A current replica counts as a copy off the premises** in 3-2-1, not as a backup.

### What's new after an update

- **Green dots mark what changed**, also on the tabs and tiles that lead there. A click hides a dot, and **New** lists every change with **Go there**.

### First start

- **A welcome page** with what BombVault has found, the three steps to the first backup, and the way to restore from an existing backup.

## 🎨 Changed

### Navigation

- **The sidebar has five entries**: Overview, Backups, Restore, Anomalies and Settings. Storage locations and Instances are settings tiles that can be pinned to the sidebar.
- **Pages start with their content.** There are no page headings, and a page's main action floats at the bottom right.
- **Sign out stands above Settings**, and a count in the sidebar wears the colour of its entry.
- **On a phone** the bar holds four entries and **More**.

### Settings

- **Fourteen tiles**: General, Appearance, Schedule, Storage locations, Restore, Notifications, Verify, Security, Instances, Pairing, Connections, Apps, System and Info.
- **A search over all of them**, opened with `/` or Ctrl+K. It also finds the names pages had before.
- **Info** holds About, Version and Help. Version lists BombVault, GlimStone, restic and rclone with **Check for updates**, and Help has the bug report.
- **Nothing folds out, and there is no Simple or Advanced switch.** Rare things have a card of their own or a window, and explanations sit in info bubbles.

### Storage locations

- **One place for local and off-site.** A location is added from provider tiles and has a page of its own with its connection, retention, copy, delete protection and rclone fields.
- **Retention as Short, Balanced, Long or Custom**, with a question before a shorter rule deletes backups.
- **Own choice** lists only the entries that back up somewhere else than their section, each with **Use the default**.

### Schedule

- **Schedules read as sentences**, such as *Weekly on Sunday at 04:00*, and are edited from that sentence.
- **Days are spelled out** wherever there is room.

### Details

- **Container registries** are added from tiles with their logos.
- **Number fields** have plain arrows.
- **A new logo**, orange warnings, five type sizes and GlimStone 3.4.0.

## 🌐 Translations

- The new interface in all 42 languages and the documentation in all 26.

## Upgrading

- **Nothing has to be changed.** Old links lead to the new pages, and an overview you arranged keeps its cards.
